short: Insights into the Distinct Lithiation/Sodiation of Porous Co
title: Insights into the Distinct Lithiation/Sodiation of Porous Cobalt Oxide by in Operando Synchrotron X-ray Techniques and Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics Simulations

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Why cobalt oxide stores lithium well but sodium badly has not been resolved at the structural level. Watching one porous cobalt oxide cycle against Li and against Na in operando should locate where sodiation fails.
states.detail: Absorbed: n2 (HYP/gap), n3 (HYP/hypothesis), n4 (DES/base_system), n5 (DES/route), n6 (DES/method), n7 (DES/variable_sweep), n8 (PRC/synthesis), n9 (PRC/stimulus)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: The product is a two-phase mixture of cubic Co3O4 (Fd-3m) and cubic CoO (Fm-3m), about 79:21 by weight. Lithiation drives the crystalline oxide fully amorphous and charging does not bring the crystallinity back.
states.detail: Absorbed: n10 (STR/phase/identity), n14 (STR/phase/fraction), n15 (STR/phase/fraction), n16 (STR/chemistry/composition), n17 (STR/chemistry/composition), n18 (STR/microstructure/porosity). Premises: Co foil, CoO and Co3O4 standards fix where the Co K-edge and its FT shells sit for each valence; Mesoporous Co3O4 in LIBs is known to recharge to CoO rather than back to Co3O4

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Against lithium: 1330 mA h/g first discharge, 871 reversible, still ~850 after 40 cycles. Against sodium: 866 mA h/g first discharge but only 472 reversible, decaying to ~65 by cycle 40.

states.title: Performance state
states.head: The porous oxide serves as a good lithium-ion anode and a poor sodium-ion anode

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Poor sodium storage in cobalt oxide is a limit of the Na-O conversion chemistry, not of the pore architecture

nodes.title: XRD:synchrotron, F1
nodes.head: Rietveld calculated pattern sits on the observed one with a flat difference curve; weights are 78.6% Co3O4 and 21.4% CoO
nodes.solves: The product is a two-phase mixture of cubic Co3O4 (Fd-3m) and cubic CoO (Fm-3m), about 79:21 by weight
nodes.note: weights are printed in F1a; both Co3O4 and CoO tick rows are needed to account for the peaks, and the residual shows only small misfits at 2.7 and 4.4 deg
nodes.necessity_reason: n10 keeps shown support from o2 after removal.

nodes.title: XRD:synchrotron, F4
nodes.head: Li cell: the 16.4 and 19.2 deg reflections fade to a flat trace part way down the discharge and never reappear on charge. Na cell: the 16.4, 19.2 and 20.1 deg reflections persist through the whole cycle, only slightly weaker and not shifted
nodes.solves: Lithiation drives the crystalline oxide fully amorphous and charging does not bring the crystallinity back
nodes.note: in F4a the peaks are already gone by about 5 h, near 1 V, not only at the 0.01 V endpoint the text names F4b covers 16-21 deg; the intensity at the end of charge is below the pristine trace but the peaks are intact
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n14, n15 (o9, o10).

nodes.title: XAS:EXAFS, F5
nodes.head: Li cell: the Co white line collapses and moves towards Co foil, and the FT shell moves from 1.48/2.48 to a single ~2.1 A peak. Na cell: all cycled XANES curves stay bunched near the pristine trace and the FT keeps its two Co3O4 shells throughout
nodes.solves: Lithiation reduces Co towards the metal; recharging returns it only to a CoO-like state, not to pristine PCO
nodes.note: F5b: the 1st and 2nd charge curves lie on the CoO reference, not on the OCV curve; F5e shows the Co3O4 double shell replaced by one Co-Co shell at the bottom of discharge F5d is the Na/PCO XANES. The cycled curves (1st/2nd discharge and charge) are bunched at a white line of ~1.30 and sit essentially on the Co3O4 reference; the OCV trace is sharper (~1.49) and slightly higher in energy, so sodiation does change the edge somewhat, but nothing moves towards the Co-foil edge. F5f keeps the two Co3O4 shells at 1.56 and 2.48 A.
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n16, n17 (o11, o12).

nodes.title: THERMAL:TGA, F1
nodes.head: Weight falls to 95.8 wt% between about 250 and 420 C, then creeps back to ~96.3% by 800 C
nodes.note: 95.8 wt% is the label printed on the F1b plateau; the slow gain above 500 C is not mentioned in the text
nodes.detail: o2: Weight falls to 95.8 wt% between about 250 and 420 C, then creeps back to ~96.3% by 800 C
nodes.necessity_reason: n10 keeps shown support from o1 after removal.

nodes.title: XRD:SAXS, F3
nodes.head: SAXS: in the Li cell low-q intensity falls and moves to lower q while high-q intensity rises, and neither returns on charge
nodes.solves: Lithiation fills the large pores and creates new fine scatterers, and neither recovers on charge
nodes.note: contours read from F3a and F3c against the co-plotted voltage curve; in F3b the 0.02 V Li trace falls below OCV at low q and grows a bump near q = 0.2, and the 3 V trace does not return, while the Na traces in F3d superimpose at every state
nodes.detail: o8: SAXS: in the Li cell low-q intensity falls and moves to lower q while high-q intensity rises, and neither returns on charge
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n18 (o8).

nodes.title: SEM, F1
nodes.head: SEM at 70k shows interconnected rough blocks of ~100-200 nm; the 10-20 nm particles claimed in the text are not resolved
nodes.note: sized against the 500 nm bar (OCR cue) in F1d; surface texture is visible but individual nanograins are not
nodes.necessity_reason: No member reaches image_support shown, and n12 keeps shown support from o3, o5, o6.

nodes.title: ATOM:MD, F6
nodes.head: AIMD snapshots: Li pulls oxygen out and disorders the Co3O4 slab; Na leaves it ordered but does disorder the Co3S4 slab
nodes.solves: Sodium cannot strip oxygen from Co3O4 and stays largely un-oxidised, whereas it does attack the softer sulfide sublattice
nodes.note: compared frame by frame from 0.2 to 2.0 ps in F6a, F6b and F6c; in F6b only the topmost oxygen row moves
nodes.necessity_reason: n20 keeps shown support from o14 after removal.

nodes.title: PHYS:surfacearea, F1
nodes.head: Type IV isotherm with a high-pressure hysteresis loop reaching ~112 cm3/g; the pore-size inset is bimodal near 5.5 and 6.7 nm
nodes.note: read from the F1c axes and its pore-size inset, which runs only to 10 nm
nodes.detail: o3: Type IV isotherm with a high-pressure hysteresis loop reaching ~112 cm3/g; the pore-size inset is bimodal near 5.5 and 6.7 nm
nodes.necessity_reason: n12 keeps shown support from o5, o6 after removal.

nodes.title: ECHEM:galvanostatic, F2
nodes.head: Li cell first discharge ends at ~1330 mA h/g after a long 1.05 V plateau; first charge returns ~870 on a 2.0 V plateau. Li capacity climbs from ~870 to ~1090 mA h/g by cycle 17 and then falls back to ~850 at cycle 40, at ~95% efficiency
nodes.solves: Against lithium: 1330 mA h/g first discharge, 871 reversible, still ~850 after 40 cycles
nodes.note: read from the F2a capacity axis; the 40th discharge curve has lost the low plateau and ends near 850 read from F2b; the quoted 96.4% retention compares cycle 40 with cycle 1 and hides the rise and fall
nodes.detail: o5: Li cell first discharge ends at ~1330 mA h/g after a long 1.05 V plateau; first charge returns ~870 on a 2.0 V plateau; o6: Li capacity climbs from ~870 to ~1090 mA h/g by cycle 17 and then falls back to ~850 at cycle 40, at ~95% efficiency
nodes.necessity_reason: n12 keeps shown support from o3 after removal.

nodes.head: Na cell gives ~866 mA h/g first discharge but only ~470 charge, and decays monotonically to ~65 mA h/g by cycle 40

nodes.detail: o7: Na cell gives ~866 mA h/g first discharge but only ~470 charge, and decays monotonically to ~65 mA h/g by cycle 40
